subject: Network telemetry handshake & streaming tail-latency alignment
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Lisa Moreno <lisa@climesense.io>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference, karthik.iyer@redwood.inference
Date: Thu, 28 Apr 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Network telemetry handshake & streaming tail-latency alignment
Attachments: redwood_net_checklist.csv (csv)

Hi Lisa — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the concrete asks we discussed so the teams can move fast: 

Summary of performance goals you called out
- Streaming tail-latency budget: 99.9th <= 300ms end-to-end (from packet egress at customer edge to streamed-first-byte delivered to client).
- Per-token/segment latency target during steady-state: ~150–200ms (we'll validate server-side hotspot).
- Concurrency: baseline 150 active streams, expected bursts up to 300 for 30–60s windows.
- Throughput: target sustained request-rate equivalent to ~4k tokens/sec across the cluster for the POC.
- Success criteria: >=95% streaming sessions with no frame re-order or truncation; packet loss <0.5% during test windows.

Presumed network path and constraints we discussed
- Egress via your on-prem firewall -> VPN peering to us-west-2 (customer-managed VPN).
- No public NAT hairpinning if possible; prefer a peer-based route.
- TLS termination: on Redwood side (we currently support mutual TLS to secure control plane).

Asks / next steps
1) Please share the network owner(s) and a contact for your infra team to schedule a connectivity preflight.
2) Can you confirm whether UDP streaming is acceptable, or must the stream ride over HTTP/2 / WebSocket (TCP)? This changes packetization expectations.
3) Propose a 2-week POC window — suggested start Mon May 10. Are you available for that window?
4) I attached a short net-checklist (redwood_net_checklist.csv). If your infra team can populate fields, we can pre-run simulated tests.

I'll loop Vanessa on the technical runbook after the topology doc is shared. Happy to jump on a quick 30-minute handoff with your network/security folks.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

From: Lisa Moreno <lisa@climesense.io>

Cc: procurement@climesense.io, security@climesense.io
Date: Thu, 28 Apr 2027 18:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Network telemetry handshake & streaming tail-latency alignment

Thanks, Jonas — helpful summary. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 99.9th <= 300ms is tight but reasonable if we keep the number of hops predictable. Our internal hop budget from app edge -> peering is 40–60ms depending on routing.
- The stream must traverse our perimeter firewall (we use an on-prem F/W cluster running TLS passthrough today). We do prefer TCP (WebSocket/HTTP2) for auditability and because our proxies currently do not forward UDP to external peers.
- Procurement: will need a scoped MSA + PO terms before we authorize the POC (looping them here).
- Security: need SOC2 artifacts and a short list of telemetry we'll share (packet captures are allowed under NDA during the test window).

I attached our topology draft (I will upload the canonical file to the Drive link) and have asked our network contact (Mike) to reach out. Please include a short list of IP ranges and sample ports you will open so I can get the firewall change request started.

Lisa Moreno
CTO, ClimeSense
lisa@climesense.io

Hi all — quick technical follow-up from our infra readiness side. Thanks for the topology, Lisa; a couple of clarifying items so we can design the test harness: 

1) Protocols and ports- We can run streaming over HTTP/2 (gRPC-web / h2) or raw WebSocket; we do not require UDP. Please confirm you are OK with TCP-only streaming (your note suggests yes). If so, we'll provide a sample URL and authority header for the firewall rule.

2) TLS and mTLS- We can do mutual TLS for the control channel (API calls that provision the session) and TLS for the actual media stream. If you prefer TLS passthrough at your edge, we'll need a guaranteed 5–10s window for TLS renegotiation tests during the POC to validate session resumption.

3) Telemetry we need from your side during tests- 1s granularity RTT measurements at the peering/device, packet-loss counters, and a periodic p95/p99 tail-latency log for client-facing SDK timers. I've attached telemetry-sample.json to show the fields we’ll consume.

4) Pre-flight measurements (recommended)
- iperf3 baseline (10s windows, both directions)
- 60s jitter test with stepwise concurrency (50, 150, 300)
- 5-minute ramp that includes an artificial burst of 600 concurrent session attempts to validate graceful degradation and queueing behavior

5) Acceptance thresholds we suggest to start- p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 275ms, p99.9 <= 350ms during burst windows (we'll tune once we see real path latency). Packet-loss target <0.5% sustained.

If that's agreeable, we can publish a POC runbook (checklist + test scripts) and propose the May 10 start that Jonas suggested. Also, please send the firewall change request with the CIDR ranges below (we'll provide exact ranges once you confirm TCP-only):
- example: 34.200.100.0/24 (Redwood control)
- example: 34.201.101.0/24 (Redwood streaming egress)

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-minute network-level call if Mike prefers.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_v1.md (md)

Great — thanks everyone for the quick alignment. Below is a short mutual action plan (MAP) to lock dates and success criteria. Please respond with any edits and confirm the network owner for the firewall ticket.

Mutual Action Plan (high-level)
- POC window: May 10 – May 24 (2 weeks)
- Pre-flight week: May 3–7 (topology validation + firewall rule change + iperf baseline)
- Test plan: incremental concurrency ramp (50 -> 150 -> 300) with two burst tests (300 -> 600 attempt spike for 30–60s)
- Acceptance criteria:
  • Sustained throughput: >= 4k tokens/sec equivalent across cluster during steady-state ramp.
  • Concurrency support: 150 sustained active streams with successful bursts to 300 without systemic failures.
  • Latency: p95 <= 200ms, p99 <= 275ms, p99.9 <= 350ms during test windows; tail events investigated if outside thresholds.
  • Observability: 1s-gran RTT and packet-loss metrics, server-side KV cache hit-rate logs, and 5-minute sampling of packet captures under NDA for root cause analysis.
- Security & compliance: we will provide SOC2 artifacts and a short data-flow diagram; ClimeSense will provide an NDA for packet-capture exchanges.
- Commercials: procurement to provide PO or countersigned MSA before the Pre-flight week.

Action items (owners)
- ClimeSense (Lisa/Mike): post topology to the Drive link, open firewall change request, nominate network contact.
- Redwood (Vanessa): publish test scripts + telemetry schema by May 1.
- Redwood (Jonas): send DocuSign for POC statement of work and kick off calendar invites.

DocuSign: https://docusign.net/Envelopes/ABC123-climesense-poc
Drive topology: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-climesense-topology

Please reply with confirmation. If no objections, we'll treat this MAP as the working plan and lock the pre-flight week.
